note: The missing-GROUP-BY repair (#73). Read the attribution before quoting the headline: of the +7 attempts, +5 are the repair (group_by 22/27 -> 27/27) and +2 are the two known-flaky date cases both landing well this round. The repair cannot touch the date category, so the attributable gain is +5 attempts = +2.9 points. A round where those two date cases fall the other way would read ~92.4% with this same code.

previous.note: After the date period repair (#69). group_by was 22/27.

known_failures.note: Exactly three cases fail, each 0/3, and each has a named issue. Five categories are now at 100%. Every remaining failure is a semantic choice the SQL cannot reveal — which is why all three resisted the deterministic approach that fixed #52, #58, #69 and #73.

always_failing.sales_cheapest_product: #59 — returns the measure, not the entity: SELECT MIN(price) instead of the product. A repair would have to guess which column is the entity; the AST does not carry it.
always_failing.sales_laptop_units: #60 — COUNT(CASE WHEN ...) counts orders (3) where SUM(quantity) was meant (11). Both readings of 'how many' are legitimate; only the schema breaks the tie.
always_failing.sales_products_over_200k: #74 — a per-group threshold ('products generating more than 200000 in revenue') becomes a row-level WHERE instead of GROUP BY + HAVING SUM(...).

known_failures.flaky_note: emp_joined_2021 and sales_march_revenue passed 3/3 this round but were 2/3 last round; neither is the #69 defect (one invents an upper bound, one emits LIKE '%03-2024%'). Treat date as ~13-15/15, not a solid 15.

floor_rationale: Still 80, and still deliberately. Two rounds now sit at 90.6 and 94.7, but the spread between them is almost entirely two flaky date cases — which is exactly the argument against moving a CI gate on a small number of samples. `eval.yml` runs weekly; once three or more rounds exist on this code, set the floor ~6 points under the lowest observed. The floor's job is catching a category collapse, which 80 still does.
